PullRequest.Title: sessions: extend sessions list drag and drop across placements
PullRequest.Body:
Extends drag and drop in the Agents window Sessions list so that sessions can be moved between all list placements, not only into groups and Pinned.

## What changed

Every session drop now resolves to a **destination placement**: Pinned, a custom group, the session's own ungrouped section (workspace, Recent/Older, Chats, External), or Archived, plus an optional anchor row. A single move function then applies only the state that the list's placement precedence (archived > pinned > group > section) needs: archive or unarchive, pin or unpin, join or leave a group, and the manual sort key. Adding a drop target is one more case that maps the hovered element to a destination. Adding a placement is one more entry in `getPlacementState`.

New behaviors:
- **Out of a group into date sections**: grouped sessions can be dragged back into Recent/Older (and grouped quick chats back into Chats).
- **Unpin by dragging**: drop a pinned session on its own section or between that section's sessions.
- **Archive / unarchive by dragging**: dropping on the archived section archives the sessions with the existing "N archived · Undo" notification, through a new internal `sessionsViewPane.archiveSessionsWithUndo` command. Archived sessions dropped on a section, group, or Pinned are restored first.
- **Date header drops**: dropping on Recent or Older places sessions at the top of that section. When the gap crosses the Recent/Older boundary, keys stay next to the anchor so the session lands in the highlighted section.
- **Drop on empty space** (date grouping): sessions go to the end of the date sections. Archived sessions are refused.
- **Chat rows**: nested chats can be reordered within their session. This stores a new persisted, list-owned chat order per sort mode in `ISessionsListModelService`; chats missing from the order keep their natural position. Dropping a session on a chat row places it after that chat's session.

Side effects: comparison groups are no longer offered as targets for membership changes (those drops used to look valid but do nothing). Reorder neighbours now come from all sessions in the anchor's sort scope instead of only visible rows, so drops also work against collapsed sections.

`SESSIONS_LIST.md` is updated because the drag-and-drop contract and the persisted list state changed.

## How to test

In the Agents window Sessions list:
1. Group by date. Drag a session out of a custom group onto a Recent/Older row, onto the Older header, and below the last row.
2. Drag a pinned session onto its own section, and drag a session onto the Done/Archived header (check Undo).
3. With archived sessions shown, drag an archived session onto Recent.
4. Expand a session with nested chats, reorder them, and switch sort modes.

## Validation

- `tsc` type check of the changed files: no errors in `src/vs/sessions` (run with the main checkout's TypeScript because this worktree's `node_modules` could not be reinstalled).
- Unit tests in `src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts` were added and updated but **not run locally**; CI will run them.
- ESLint was **not run locally**.
- The chat reorder has no keyboard equivalent yet; the other moves already have context-menu actions.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call path and unthrottled event forwarding are explicit, and both collection-wide sorts are directly visible. Exact catalog sizes vary by user, so magnitude is uncertain, but session history is persistent and Older is not capped.
Findings.PerformanceResource: main-thread CPU work and temporary arrays/maps from full-tree traversal, filtering, and sorting
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For every native dragover event over a date-section destination, cost grows as O(T + N log N): sortInDisplayOrder traverses the rendered tree T, computeSessionReorder filters and sorts the full session catalog N, and this line copies/sorts/groups all date sessions again. The work repeats at pointer-event frequency while hovering.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased drag latency and dropped frames in large session histories
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Dragover validated the target with placement and selection predicates; the collection-wide scope filtering/sort used to compute synthetic sort keys ran only when the user dropped the sessions.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Date-section dragover now predicts final placement by traversing the tree, sorting the full reorder scope, then copying, sorting, and regrouping all date sessions before accepting each hover event.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added dragover resolver calls getSessionDropEffect for every hover event; its new rendersInDateSection path reaches added line 5815, while the deleted implementation only performed target/selection predicates during dragover and deferred reorder scope construction to reorderSessions on drop.
Findings.Title: Avoid rebuilding date placement on every dragover
Findings.Impact: With date grouping and a long-lived catalog, dragging over a Recent/Older row or header repeatedly performs two collection sorts plus a full tree walk on the UI thread, making the insertion feedback and pointer movement stutter.
Findings.Evidence: SessionsListDragAndDrop.onDragOver synchronously calls resolveDrop -> resolveSessionDrop -> getSessionDropEffect -> rendersInDateSection. At lines 5810-5815 that path invokes sortInDisplayOrder, computeSessionReorder (lines 5901+ filters and sorts this.sessions), and sortSessions/groupByDate. The base list forwards native dragover events directly without throttling. SessionsList.refresh assigns this.sessions from getSessions(), so the reorder sort uses the uncapped provider catalog; date grouping also retains all non-Recent sessions in Older.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep dragover validation lightweight: cache the predicted date placement/reorder context by list-model revision, dragged IDs, and destination (or compute it once per target), invalidate it when sessions/order/grouping change, and perform the authoritative full recomputation once on drop.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drag one or more sessions across Recent/Older rows or date-section headers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Native dragover synchronously resolves the destination and validates predicted date placement before feedback can update. The new validation traverses the tree, builds and sorts the full reorder scope, then sorts and regroups date sessions; all of it is on the UI critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Uncapped provider session catalog N, date-section sessions D, rendered tree nodes T including nested chats, selected sessions K, multiplied by native dragover event frequency. Effective cardinality is not reduced by workspace per-group limits because this.sessions comes directly from getSessions(), and Older retains all remaining date sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded and serialized on the renderer UI thread; list dragover forwarding has no throttle, coalescing, or memoization.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or coalescing exists for dragged IDs, target destination, reorder scope, or predicted date grouping, so identical hover events repeat all work. Cold and warm behavior are equivalent until the model changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the direct dragover call path and both collection-wide sorts/full-tree traversal are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact session-history and nested-chat sizes vary, but persistent histories can make N and T large; this affects severity, not the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity synchronous UI regression because collection-wide work newly repeats at pointer-event frequency; one finding submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drop selected sessions into Pinned, a custom group, their ungrouped section, or Archived
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On drop, display order is captured; placement changes then complete in precedence order. Archive invokes the command and provider operations before completion; restoring archived sessions awaits each provider unarchive before pin/group/sort state is applied.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Archive each selected active session through ISessionsManagementService and the owning sessions provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to K provider archive calls, serialized; only non-archived candidates are included.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Drag/drop did not archive sessions, while the existing archive action already used the same serialized helper and per-session provider calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the drop operation and undo notification complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Unarchive each selected archived session through ISessionsManagementService and the owning provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized call per selected archived session; active sessions make no call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This drag destination did not exist; the pre-existing multi-session Restore action also serialized the same provider calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each call is awaited before pin/group/order mutations proceed; remote/dev-container providers can perform IPC, connection setup, or detached-worktree operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist pin/manual sort changes through ISessionsListModelService
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Pin can be per changed session; unpin and sort changes are batched by the service, with at most one sort persistence for the drop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing pin/group/reorder drops used the same owning services and persistence mechanisms.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous state/storage work occurs during the drop but not during hover.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Selected session count K after list selection deduplication. Archive/unarchive boundary calls are one per selected session that actually changes archived state; pin/group/sort work is bounded by K plus one batched group/sort update.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Archive and restore provider calls are deliberately serialized. Group joining and sort persistence are batched; unpin/group removal can emit per-session state changes depending on owning services.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache applies to mutations. Current archive/pin/group state avoids operations for sessions already in the destination state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call count and serialization; provider-specific latency varies.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large multi-selection drops and slow remote/dev-container providers are less common, and serialization preserves ordering/error/undo semantics already used by existing actions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the diff adds valid drag routes, but the per-item provider semantics match existing batch actions and no safe parallel alternative is established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reorder nested chats by drag, keyboard, or provider-owned move
Scenarios.CriticalPath: List-owned reorder computes the current sibling order, persists one per-session order, emits a model event, and rebuilds the visible list. Provider-owned moves first clear conflicting list-owned order and then invoke the existing provider move asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and store all manual chat-order maps after a changed list-owned reorder
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write per accepted drag drop or keyboard move; serialized payload spans all sessions with manual chat orders in both sort modes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No list-owned nested-chat order existed, so there was no corresponding persistence write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous before the model change event and list rebuild complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Move/reorder a provider-owned chat using the existing sessions-list move operation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider move per gesture; no per-chat fan-out is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider-movable chat drag/drop already used this move path; the diff adds keyboard routing and clears conflicting local order.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and off the immediate drop handler after local conflict cleanup; reveal waits for provider/model updates.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Chats C in the affected session and total persisted manual-order entries P. A list-owned gesture is O(C) plus serialization of P; provider-owned moves touch source/destination order entries only. Rendering applies ordering only to sessions with stored orders and scales with each session's chat count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous storage/model update per list-owned gesture. Provider move remains asynchronous; clearing source/destination orders can emit sequential updates only when such orders actually exist.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Orders load once into maps at service construction and reads are warm O(1) by session ID. Equal orders skip writes; session deletion clears both sort-mode entries. No negative cache issue was found.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for local serialization and event behavior; storage backend flush timing and provider latency are implementation-dependent.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Nested chat counts and the number of sessions users manually reorder are expected to be modest; key-repeat can increase frequency but payload remains user-history bounded and cleanup exists.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: work is bounded to explicit reorder gestures, equal writes are suppressed, deleted-session state is cleaned, and provider call cardinality does not increase.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh the Sessions list with persisted nested-chat orders
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The model service parses stored order state once at construction. Each visible list rebuild naturally sorts chats, then applies a stored order for sessions that have one before creating tree children.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse persisted nested-chat order state during service construction
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One profile-storage read and JSON parse per service lifetime, independent of list rebuild count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The chat-order storage key did not exist or load.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs during service initialization before order lookups are available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Persisted ordered sessions P and chats C per session; list rebuild cost is the sum of per-session chat ordering, with no remote calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous list-model construction and UI rebuild; no parallel work or queueing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Parsed orders are retained in maps for warm O(1) lookups. Missing orders return undefined and avoid extra allocation/sorting in applyManualChatOrder. Session deletion invalidates persisted entries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Persisted payload size depends on explicit user reorders but is cleaned when sessions are deleted.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: one-time parsing and warm map lookups are bounded by explicit persisted user state, with cleanup and lazy per-session ordering.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files and all paginated diff pages. Submitted one medium synchronous-UI finding for uncached full-list recomputation on every date-section dragover; inspected mutation/provider/storage boundaries and found no other high-confidence diff-caused regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
